free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'AWS Educate is open to any individual, regardless of where they are in their education, technical experience, or career journey', and 'No credit card needed. Learners as young as 13 can register for AWS Educate with just an email address'. The named labs cover EC2, S3, RDS, VPC and Cloud Operations. The FAQ then defines what a lab is: 'These labs provide a simulated environment where users can interact with AWS services, experiment with different configurations, and apply theoretical knowledge to solve practical problems.'

egress.terms: Nothing binds because nothing is provisioned: the EC2 and S3 exercises run in a simulated console, so there is no quota to exhaust, no egress to meter and no wall clock that ends with a resource to lose.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The one program in this class whose identity gate a user passes outright; it is the only door that stays open without enrollment documents, but what it opens is a lab, not an account.

identity_cost.detail: email only: the vendor page states "No credit card needed. Learners as young as 13 can register for AWS Educate with just an email address" and the learner FAQ states "There is no need to provide credit card information"; the registration form asks for first and last name, country, city, birth month and year and an email address, with no enrollment document anywhere on it. No card, no hold, and debit or prepaid do not arise because no payment method is taken

evidence.proved: 'No credit card needed. Learners as young as 13 can register for AWS Educate with just an email address', and 'AWS Educate is open to any individual, regardless of where they are in their education, technical experience, or career journey'.

'These labs provide a simulated environment where users can interact with AWS services, experiment with different configurations'; 'All our courses are absolutely free, including access to labs'; 'There is no need to provide credit card information'.

Registration requires first and last name, country, city, birth month and year, and an email address; the only program question is which AWS program the learner is associated with, and 'AWS Educate' is one of three options. No enrollment document is requested anywhere on the form.

notes: Refutation. AWS Educate is the one program in this class whose identity gate a user passes outright, an email address and nothing else, which makes it the most attractive name on every student-list article; the vendor FAQ says the EC2, S3 and RDS labs are a simulated environment rather than an AWS account, so the practical compute is zero. The FAQ corrected it. The FAQ does not state a lab session length or any per-lab allowance, and there is nothing to measure because no real resource is provisioned. Separately, the Job Board retires on 9 December 2026 and the Emerging Talent Community moves to AWS Builder Center, so the non-lab part of the program is also contracting.
